title: Sales channel intake scorer and initial scope sketch for enterprise feature requests
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create an automated Sales/CS-facing intake aggregator that consolidates enterprise feature asks into a normalized ticket, assigns a product-fit and cost score, and emits a one-page initial scope sketch for PM/Eng review. The goal is to reduce manual triage time, give consistent answers to Sales on feasibility/econ, and surface high-value cross-account feature signals for roadmap consideration.
background_and_motivation: Sales and Customer Success increasingly submit long free-text asks into multiple channels (HubSpot, email, Slack, support tickets). PMs spend ~4 hours per request to normalize, check infra constraints, and provide a back-of-envelope cost/priority assessment. This creates slow responses to prospects and inconsistent prioritization. We need an intake layer that automates normalization, standardizes scoring, and produces an initial scope + recommended next step (POC, design spike, backlog, or decline).
outcome_metrics: 1) Reduce PM triage time per request from ~4h to <=30m for 80% of requests. 2) Time-to-first-response to Sales under 48h for qualifying asks. 3) Increase discoverable cross-account signal groups by 2x in 90 days. 4) Generate estimated infra delta (GPU hours/month) for 90% of requests.
acceptance_criteria: Sales can submit an ask via Slack slash command or HubSpot form and receive a normalized ticket in Linear automatically
Automated scorer outputs product-fit (0-10), implementation-complexity (0-10), infra-cost-tier (low/medium/high), and recommended action
Generated one-page scope sketch (template) attached to the ticket including: business context, success metrics, a 3-line solution sketch, rough infra estimate, and next-step recommendation
PM/Eng can override any automated fields and add final disposition; audit log of overrides captured
Dashboard shows request volume, top themes, average score, and triage time reduction after rollout
proposed_flow_steps: 1) Sales/CS submits ask via HubSpot form or Slack slash-command -> payload normalized (account, ARR, contact, brief, priority)
2) NLP normalizer extracts intent, entities, and maps to existing signal clusters using fuzzy matching
3) Scoring engine computes product-fit, complexity, and infra-cost-tier using heuristics and historical priors
4) System generates one-page scope sketch (Markdown) and creates Linear ticket in PM queue with tags and fields
5) PM triages ticket; if auto-score >= threshold and infra-cost acceptable -> assign to discovery or schedule POC; else route back to Sales with standardized reply template
scoring_logic_summary: Product-fit := weighted sum( strategic-alignment(0-5), potential-revenue(0-5), frequency-of-ask(0-5) ) normalized to 0-10. Complexity := model-change(0-4) + infra-change(0-3) + console-work(0-3). Infra-cost-tier uses model type, expected QPS, and batchability heuristics to map to low/medium/high. We will seed priors from last 18 months of closed requests and adjust with PM feedback.
integration_points: Slack slash-command -> normalizer (ephemeral confirmation to submitter)
Linear API -> create/update ticket with auto-populated fields
Redwood Console dashboards -> heatmap of themes & triage metrics
Confluence/Drive link field for supporting attachments
risks_and_tradeoffs: Automated scoring may introduce false negatives for creative requests; to mitigate, we will include a low-effort 'flag for manual review' trigger and monitor false-negative rate for the first 6 weeks. Integrations add operational surface area: prefer HubSpot webhook + Slack command rollout before expanding to email parsing. Scoring relies on historical priors — new enterprise verticals may need manual seeding.
design_and_ux_notes: One-page scope sketch template must be sales-friendly (single page PDF or Markdown), include a clear CTA for Sales (POC, estimate, decline), and a short canned reply templates for Sales reps. PMs should be able to edit template fields inline in Linear.
engineering_notes: MVP components: normalizer service (small Flask/Node service), scoring service (Python service with lightweight ML features), Linear create/update job, and Console dashboard ingestion. Keep services stateless; persist priors and overrides in existing product-intake datastore. Start with rule-backed heuristics; phase ML retraining in Phase 2.
